title: SAC 8-Day Airstrike Campaign in Chin State Kills 29 — 20 Civilians (Including Children) and 9 Resistance Fighters
detail: Myanmar junta forces conducted a sustained eight-day airstrike campaign across Chin State that killed a total of 29 people — 20 civilians including children and 9 members of resistance forces — according to data compiled by the Mizzima Spring Revolution Daily News for May 11, 2026. The campaign is part of the broader SAC military operation in Chin State that has intensified following the junta's recapture of Falam (April 25-26) and Kennedy Peak in Tedim Township (May 7). Documented individual strikes within the campaign include: the May 8 bombing of Phunom village, Tedim Township (7 PDF-Zoland fighters and 3 civilians killed); the May 6 airstrike on Phunon village in Tedim (9 PDF members killed, including 5 women and 4 men); and a May 7 strike on a hospital in Winmana village, Kani Township. The 29-casualty cumulative tally in just 8 days makes this among the deadliest concentrated airstrike campaigns in Chin State since the coup. The junta is deploying both jet aircraft and armed drones against resistance positions and civilian areas, following its recapture of the Falam-Tedim corridor. Chin State — one of the most mountainous and accessible-only-by-difficult-roads regions of Myanmar — has limited independent media access, meaning the true casualty count is likely higher. The SAC's systematic bombing of civilian areas in the Chin Hills constitutes deliberate targeting of non-military populations under international humanitarian law, adding to the pattern documented by ACLED of 2,602 air attacks in 2025 (the highest annual rate since the coup).

media.caption: Eight-day SAC airstrike campaign in Chin State kills 29 — 20 civilians including children and 9 resistance fighters — Mizzima Spring Revolution Daily News, May 11, 2026

title: SAC Airstrikes Drive Mass Evacuation of 10+ Villages in Kani Township, Sagaing Region
detail: Junta airstrikes in the west and northwest areas of Kani Township, Sagaing Region, that began May 7, 2026, have forced residents of no fewer than 10 villages to evacuate their homes, according to Mizzima Spring Revolution Daily News for May 11. The Kani Township strikes follow a May 7 airstrike on a hospital in Winmana village (Kani Township, Sagaing Region) where two PDF members receiving medical treatment were killed. The scale of displacement — 10+ villages forced to evacuate in one township alone — reflects the junta's strategy of depopulating resistance-aligned areas through sustained aerial bombardment to deny the PDF its civilian support base and logistical infrastructure. Kani Township in Sagaing Region has been an active combat zone throughout 2025-2026 as PDF forces have operated throughout Sagaing. The displacement of thousands from 10+ villages in Kani adds to an already catastrophic internal displacement crisis: UN OCHA counted 3.6 million IDPs in Myanmar as of November 2025, of which Sagaing Region accounts for one of the largest concentrations. Displaced civilians from Kani have no access to formal camps and are sheltering in forests, temples, and neighboring villages, with inadequate food, medicine, or shelter during the hot season. Deaths from heatstroke among displaced persons have been reported in Sagaing and Mandalay Region in May 2026.

media.caption: SAC airstrikes in Kani Township, Sagaing Region force 10+ villages to evacuate — hospital targeted May 7, ongoing air campaign displacing thousands — Mizzima, May 11, 2026

title: Skeletal Remains of Civilian Found After Junta Incursion in Myingyan, Mandalay — At Least 10 Beheaded Since Coup, 23 Villages Burned in April Alone
detail: The skeletal remains of U Zaw Zaw, a 46-year-old civilian who went missing during a Myanmar junta troop incursion in October 2025, were discovered on May 7 beneath a mango tree in Kansint (North) Village, Myingyan Township, Mandalay Region, according to Mizzima reporting on May 11, 2026. Local residents confirmed that U Zaw Zaw's shirt, flip-flops, skeleton, and skull fragments were recovered in a scattered state consistent with his body having been left in the open. A second civilian, U Kyaw Kyaw (35), killed during the same October 2025 incursion, was found beheaded and burned inside the village. Residents reported that since the 2021 coup, approximately 10 men have been beheaded in Myingyan Township, and approximately 20 civilians have been killed during junta column incursions into the area. The broader arson campaign by junta forces has intensified in 2026: at least 23 villages in Myingyan and adjacent Taung Thar townships were burned during April alone, with some villages torched 'two or three times until homes were completely destroyed.' Displaced civilians are dying from heatstroke alongside ongoing artillery shelling and airstrikes. The killings and burnings are part of the SAC's documented counter-insurgency strategy of depopulating resistance-aligned villages in Sagaing-Mandalay Region. The pattern of beheading, burning, and abandonment of bodies constitutes extrajudicial execution and deliberate destruction of civilian property as prohibited under the 1949 Geneva Conventions.

media.caption: Skeletal remains of civilian found after October 2025 junta incursion in Myingyan Township — 10+ beheadings, 23 villages burned in April alone — Mizzima, May 11, 2026

title: Resistance Kills 8 Junta Soldiers in Myingyan Outpost Raid (Mandalay); Separate Pakokku Ambush Kills 10+ SAC Troops (Magway)
detail: Resistance forces conducted two significant operations in central Myanmar on May 11, 2026, according to the MoeMaKa CDM Domestic News. In the first operation, resistance forces raided a junta outpost in Myingyan Township, Mandalay Region, killing eight SAC soldiers and injuring nine more while withdrawing without reported resistance casualties. Myingyan Township has seen escalating junta arson and column incursions alongside sustained resistance counteroperations — the May 11 outpost raid follows days of CDF/PDF operations in the area and demonstrates that resistance forces retain operational capacity even as the SAC attempts to depopulate villages in the township. In the second operation, resistance forces ambushed a junta military column of approximately 500 soldiers in Pakokku Township, Magway Region, killing at least 10 SAC troops. Pakokku District has been an active PDF zone throughout 2025-2026. The Pakokku ambush is separate from the May 4-5 Pauk Township operation (also Magway, 9 killed) and demonstrates the PDF's ability to engage large junta columns across multiple townships simultaneously. Together, the two May 11 operations killed 18+ SAC soldiers — a significant daily tally. Junta forces injured in the Myingyan raid were transported on civilian vehicles seized from the local population, a documented SAC practice that endangers civilians and violates IHL prohibitions on using civilian property for military purposes.

media.caption: Resistance kills 8 junta soldiers in Myingyan outpost raid; separate Pakokku ambush kills 10+ SAC troops — MoeMaKa CDM News / Mizzima, May 11, 2026
